14: /-!
15: # `p`-adic Valuation
16: 
17: This file defines the `p`-adic valuation on `ℕ`, `ℤ`, and `ℚ`.
18: 
19: The `p`-adic valuation on `ℚ` is the difference of the multiplicities of `p` in the numerator and
20: denominator of `q`. This function obeys the standard properties of a valuation, with the appropriate
21: assumptions on `p`. The `p`-adic valuations on `ℕ` and `ℤ` agree with that on `ℚ`.
22: 
23: The valuation induces a norm on `ℚ`. This norm is defined in
24: `Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/PadicNorm.lean`.
25: 
26: ## Notation
27: 
28: This file uses the local notation `/.` for `Rat.mk`.
29: 
30: ## Implementation notes
31: 
32: Much, but not all, of this file assumes that `p` is prime. This assumption is inferred automatically
33: by taking `[Fact p.Prime]` as a type class argument.
34: 
35: ## Calculations with `p`-adic valuations
36: 
37: * `padicValNat_factorial`: Legendre's Theorem. The `p`-adic valuation of `n!` is the sum of the
38:   quotients `n / p ^ i`. This sum is expressed over the finset `Ico 1 b` where `b` is any bound
39:   greater than `log p n`. See `Nat.Prime.multiplicity_factorial` for the same result but stated in
40:   the language of prime multiplicity.
41: 
42: * `sub_one_mul_padicValNat_factorial`: Legendre's Theorem.  Taking (`p - 1`) times
43:   the `p`-adic valuation of `n!` equals `n` minus the sum of base `p` digits of `n`.
44: 
45: * `padicValNat_choose`: Kummer's Theorem. The `p`-adic valuation of `n.choose k` is the number
46:   of carries when `k` and `n - k` are added in base `p`. This sum is expressed over the finset
47:   `Ico 1 b` where `b` is any bound greater than `log p n`. See `Nat.Prime.multiplicity_choose` for
48:   the same result but stated in the language of prime multiplicity.
49: 
50: * `sub_one_mul_padicValNat_choose_eq_sub_sum_digits`: Kummer's Theorem. Taking (`p - 1`) times the
51:   `p`-adic valuation of the binomial `n` over `k` equals the sum of the digits of `k` plus the sum
52:   of the digits of `n - k` minus the sum of digits of `n`, all base `p`.
53: 
54: ## References
55: 
56: * [F. Q. Gouvêa, *p-adic numbers*][gouvea1997]
57: * [R. Y. Lewis, *A formal proof of Hensel's lemma over the p-adic integers*][lewis2019]
58: * <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P-adic_number>
59:

73: namespace padicValNat
74: 
75: variable {p : ℕ}
76: 
77: /-- If `p ≠ 0` and `p ≠ 1`, then `padicValNat p p` is `1`. -/
78: alias self := padicValNat_base
79: 
80: theorem eq_zero_of_not_dvd {n : ℕ} (h : ¬p ∣ n) : padicValNat p n = 0 :=
81:   eq_zero_iff.2 <| Or.inr <| Or.inr h
82: 
83: end padicValNat
84: 
85: /-- For `p ≠ 1`, the `p`-adic valuation of an integer `z ≠ 0` is the largest natural number `k` such
86: that `p^k` divides `z`. If `x = 0` or `p = 1`, then `padicValInt p q` defaults to `0`. -/
87: def padicValInt (p : ℕ) (z : ℤ) : ℕ :=
88:   padicValNat p z.natAbs
89: 
90: namespace padicValInt
91: 
92: variable {p : ℕ}
93: 
94: theorem of_ne_one_ne_zero {z : ℤ} (hp : p ≠ 1) (hz : z ≠ 0) :
95:     padicValInt p z = multiplicity (p : ℤ) z := by
96:   rw [padicValInt, padicValNat_def' hp (Int.natAbs_ne_zero.mpr hz)]
97:   apply Int.multiplicity_natAbs
98: 
99: /-- `padicValInt p 0` is `0` for any `p`. -/
100: @[simp]
101: protected theorem zero : padicValInt p 0 = 0 := by simp [padicValInt]
102: 
103: /-- `padicValInt p 1` is `0` for any `p`. -/
104: @[simp]
105: protected theorem one : padicValInt p 1 = 0 := by simp [padicValInt]
106: 
107: /-- The `p`-adic value of a natural is its `p`-adic value as an integer. -/
108: @[simp]
109: theorem of_nat {n : ℕ} : padicValInt p n = padicValNat p n := by simp [padicValInt]
110: 
111: /-- If `p ≠ 0` and `p ≠ 1`, then `padicValInt p p` is `1`. -/
112: theorem self (hp : 1 < p) : padicValInt p p = 1 := by simp [padicValNat.self hp]
113: 
114: @[simp]
115: theorem eq_zero_iff {z : ℤ} : padicValInt p z = 0 ↔ p = 1 ∨ z = 0 ∨ ¬(p : ℤ) ∣ z := by
116:   rw [padicValInt, padicValNat.eq_zero_iff, Int.natAbs_eq_zero, ← Int.ofNat_dvd_left]
117: 
118: theorem eq_zero_of_not_dvd {z : ℤ} (h : ¬(p : ℤ) ∣ z) : padicValInt p z = 0 := by
119:   simp [h]
120: 
121: end padicValInt
122: 
123: /-- `padicValRat` defines the valuation of a rational `q` to be the valuation of `q.num` minus the
124: valuation of `q.den`. If `q = 0` or `p = 1`, then `padicValRat p q` defaults to `0`. -/
125: def padicValRat (p : ℕ) (q : ℚ) : ℤ :=
126:   padicValInt p q.num - padicValNat p q.den
127: 
128: lemma padicValRat_def (p : ℕ) (q : ℚ) :
129:     padicValRat p q = padicValInt p q.num - padicValNat p q.den :=
130:   rfl
131: 
132: namespace padicValRat
133: 
134: variable {p : ℕ}
135: 
136: /-- `padicValRat p q` is symmetric in `q`. -/
137: @[simp]
138: protected theorem neg (q : ℚ) : padicValRat p (-q) = padicValRat p q := by
139:   simp [padicValRat, padicValInt]
140: 
141: /-- `padicValRat p 0` is `0` for any `p`. -/
142: @[simp]
143: protected theorem zero : padicValRat p 0 = 0 := by simp [padicValRat]
144: 
145: /-- `padicValRat p 1` is `0` for any `p`. -/
146: @[simp]
147: protected theorem one : padicValRat p 1 = 0 := by simp [padicValRat]
148: 
149: /-- The `p`-adic value of an integer `z ≠ 0` is its `p`-adic value as a rational. -/
150: @[simp]
151: theorem of_int {z : ℤ} : padicValRat p z = padicValInt p z := by simp [padicValRat]
152: 
153: /-- The `p`-adic value of an integer `z ≠ 0` is the multiplicity of `p` in `z`. -/
154: theorem of_int_multiplicity {z : ℤ} (hp : p ≠ 1) (hz : z ≠ 0) :
155:     padicValRat p (z : ℚ) = multiplicity (p : ℤ) z := by
156:   rw [of_int, padicValInt.of_ne_one_ne_zero hp hz]
157: 
158: theorem multiplicity_sub_multiplicity {q : ℚ} (hp : p ≠ 1) (hq : q ≠ 0) :
159:     padicValRat p q = multiplicity (p : ℤ) q.num - multiplicity p q.den := by
160:   rw [padicValRat, padicValInt.of_ne_one_ne_zero hp (Rat.num_ne_zero.2 hq),
161:     padicValNat_def' hp q.den_ne_zero]
162: 
163: /-- The `p`-adic value of an integer `z ≠ 0` is its `p`-adic value as a rational. -/
164: @[simp]
165: theorem of_nat {n : ℕ} : padicValRat p n = padicValNat p n := by simp [padicValRat]
166: 
167: /-- If `p ≠ 0` and `p ≠ 1`, then `padicValRat p p` is `1`. -/
168: theorem self (hp : 1 < p) : padicValRat p p = 1 := by simp [hp]
169: 
170: end padicValRat

172: section padicValNat
173: 
174: variable {p : ℕ}
175: 
176: theorem zero_le_padicValRat_of_nat (n : ℕ) : 0 ≤ padicValRat p n := by simp
177: 
178: /-- `padicValRat` coincides with `padicValNat`. -/
179: @[norm_cast]
180: theorem padicValRat_of_nat (n : ℕ) : ↑(padicValNat p n) = padicValRat p n := by simp
181: 
182: @[simp]
183: theorem padicValNat_self [Fact p.Prime] : padicValNat p p = 1 := by
184:   rw [padicValNat_def (@Fact.out p.Prime).ne_zero]
185:   simp
186: 
187: theorem one_le_padicValNat_of_dvd {n : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime] (hn : n ≠ 0) (div : p ∣ n) :
188:     1 ≤ padicValNat p n := by
189:   rwa [← ENat.coe_le_coe, padicValNat_eq_emultiplicity hn, ← pow_dvd_iff_le_emultiplicity, pow_one]
190: 
191: theorem dvd_iff_padicValNat_ne_zero {p n : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hn0 : n ≠ 0) :
192:     p ∣ n ↔ padicValNat p n ≠ 0 :=
193:   ⟨fun h => one_le_iff_ne_zero.mp (one_le_padicValNat_of_dvd hn0 h), fun h =>
194:     Classical.not_not.1 (mt padicValNat.eq_zero_of_not_dvd h)⟩
195: 
196: end padicValNat

17: In this file we define a notion of finiteness that is common in commutative algebra.

41: /-- A submodule of `M` is finitely generated if it is the span of a finite subset of `M`. -/

48:   have := h.exists_finset_coe

62:   rw [fg_def]
